## FORMAT 3

19) A format 3 INSPECT statement is interpreted and executed as though two successive INSPECT statements ...

## FORMAT 4

20) A format 4 INSPECT statement is interpreted and executed as though a format 2 INSPECT statement ...   [specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 28029 and 28033 - promoted to level-2 ATX headings, whereas every other format-applicability label in the same section is left as plain text: 'FORMATS 1 AND 3' (line ~27893 region), 'FORMATS 2 AND 3', 'FORMAT 1', 'FORMAT 4' on the page-675 slice, 'FORMATS 1 AND 2' on the page-676 slice, 'FORMAT 1', 'FORMATS 2 AND 3', 'FORMAT 2' on the page-679 slice, and 'FORMAT 2' at line 28007]
findings.why_it_matters: '## FORMAT 3' is the same heading rank as '## 14.9.22 INSPECT statement' (line 27762). Any heading-based section extraction over ISO_COBOL.md therefore terminates 14.9.22.4 General rules at rule 18 and re-parents General rules 19 through 23 (the entire normative definition of INSPECT formats 3 and 4, including EC-RANGE-INSPECT-SIZE for format 4) into two bogus top-level sections named 'FORMAT 3' and 'FORMAT 4'. A citation lookup for 14.9.22.4 GR 20 will silently miss it. The inconsistency is local and self-evident: the identical labels on the immediately preceding and following pages are plain text.
findings.suggested_repair: Demote both lines to plain body text - replace '## FORMAT 3' with 'FORMAT 3' and '## FORMAT 4' with 'FORMAT 4' at specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 28029 and 28033, matching the treatment of every other format-applicability label in 14.9.22. Sweep the other six doc-wide occurrences of a '^## FORMAT n' heading (lines 6280, 6284, 6288, 6298, 19800, 25360) and verify each against its PDF page before demoting.

findings.pdf_says: 14.9.22.4   General rules   [a fourth-level subsection of 14.9.22 INSPECT statement, printed in the same bold heading style as 14.9.21.4 General rules on page 672]
findings.markdown_says: ## 14.9.22.4 General rules [specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27892 - level 2, the same rank as '## 14.9.22 INSPECT statement' at line 27762, whereas the directly comparable '### 14.9.21.4 General rules' at line 27735 is correctly level 3 under '## 14.9.21 INITIATE statement']
findings.why_it_matters: At level 2 the General rules of INSPECT are a sibling of the INSPECT statement section rather than its child, so a heading-derived outline shows 14.9.22.4 detached from 14.9.22 and shows 14.9.22 as containing only General/General formats/Syntax rules. The neighbouring INITIATE section proves the intended level is 3, so this is an internal inconsistency, not a transcription convention.
findings.suggested_repair: Change '## 14.9.22.4 General rules' to '### 14.9.22.4 General rules' (line 27892). This is systemic, not isolated - '## 14.9.22.3 Syntax rules' (line 27853) has the same defect, as do 14.9.20.4, 14.9.24.4, 14.9.25.4, 14.9.26.4, 14.9.27.4, 14.9.28.3, 14.9.28.4 and others. Fix with one doc-wide sweep that re-levels every four-component 14.x.y.z heading to '###', not a per-page edit.
